name: Question 17
problem: A line passes through the points  $P(-3,-1,4)$ and $Q(1,8,9).$ Find its vector equation in the form $r\times v=c.$
worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-3,-1,4)$ and $Q(1,8,9).$ Now, we need to find a vector parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =q-p \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, starting with the equation of the line using the cross product, we manipulate the equation and then substitute in our values of $p$ and $v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\times v & =0 \\ r\times v-p\times v & =0 \\ r\times v & =p\times v \\ r\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ r\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & -1 & 4 \\ 4 & 9 & 5\end{aligned}\right| \\ r\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =-41i-31j+23k.\end{aligned}
$$
html:
17.?

A line passes through the points P(−3,−1,4) and Q(1,8,9). Find its vector equation in the form r×v=c.
